## This week

You posted 4 videos this week. Your typical video this week got about 1,991 views. That is down from last week, when your typical video got about 3,433 views. Your best one was "from a girl that booked $10K in her first 48 hours," which got 3,518 views. That is one of your come-up videos, the ones about how you got started. Your weakest was "one thing abt me...i'm gonna hit my 10K steps even if it means walking in circles around the airport," which only got 339 views.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?

Here is the honest answer. Across all your videos, filming style barely moves the needle. Talking to camera and voice over footage land about the same, right around your normal view count. What matters more is the topic you pick and how you build the story. You have not yet filmed the same video idea two different ways to test this directly, so there is no clean side by side proof yet. Right now, what you say and how you structure it seems to matter more than how you film it, but you have not really tested the filming style question head to head.

## What is working

Your come-up videos usually pull about twice your normal views. You have posted 28 of these, so that is a real pattern. Videos told as a full story, with a clear beginning, middle, and end, get about five times your normal views. You have posted 8 of these. And when you put a link in bio call out at the end, those videos get about 15 times your normal views. You have only done that 8 times, but it is working every time you try it.

## Try this next week

Film another how-you-got-started video, but tell it as a full story instead of a quick moment, since both of those on their own are your strongest patterns. Add a link in bio call out to your next big video, since it is pulling way more views than anything else and you have barely tested it. Try filming the exact same video idea two ways, once talking to camera and once as voice over footage, so you can finally see for yourself if filming style really matters.

best.md:
This one came in under your usual. You got 3,418 views, but a typical video from you lands closer to 4,800. For this topic though (money breakdowns like this), your past videos in that same bucket usually pull in way more, something like three and a half times your normal. So compared to what this kind of content can do for you, it underperformed hard.

Your opening line was "Breaking down EXACTLY how I made $100K w UGC." That is a strong, direct promise, it tells people exactly what they get. That part works. But the real test is seconds 3 to 6, and your script jumps straight into "my first month I took on 10 canvas UGC deals" without building any tension first. It tells, it does not tease. People need a reason to keep watching before you give away the answer.

After that, the video does keep giving reasons to stay. The month by month structure with new numbers each time is a good format, it keeps people curious about what happens next month.

You did have a call to action, but it came at the very end: "go live on Thursday." By that point most viewers are already gone. That spot almost never works.

Next time, try teasing the big number early, like "by month five I was making more than my mom's salary," then save the full breakdown for later. That gives people a reason to stay past the first 6 seconds instead of handing them the whole story up front.

worst.md:
This one did badly. You only pulled in 628 views, while a normal video of yours gets about 4,800. That is way under your usual.

Your opening line was "Here's how you turn your get ready with me videos into $10,000 without any followers." That is a strong, clear value hook, and this exact style of hook usually does well for you, pulling in more views than your normal video. So the words themselves were not the problem. Something else stopped this one from taking off, maybe timing, maybe the topic feeling repeated, maybe the caption not pulling its weight.

After the opening, you did keep giving people reasons to stay. You explained the math, named the company, broke down the deal structure, and addressed the catch, which is good pacing for a pain point to solution video.

There was no call to action in this video at all. That is a missed chance. After explaining a method this detailed, you could have told people to comment a word to get the brand list, or to follow for part two. Dropping that ask partway through, right after you explain the $10,000 math, would have been a strong spot since people are still locked in there.

Next time, add a clear call to action right after you explain the payoff, not at the end, and test whether the topic itself needs a fresher angle since the hook style usually works but this specific video did not.
